findings.title: Missing season history goes unlogged
findings.description: `season_history_for()` returns an empty `PackedByteArray` whenever the published array does not fully cover the target cell, with no `push_error`, warning, or other logging. Callers such as the info panel and cell inspector then show no history, so an incomplete publication from the background worker looks identical to a cell that simply has no history.

citations.citation: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently

evidence.explanation: The rule treats an empty result as a silent fallback and requires the missing-data path to report the cause, either through `push_error` or an explicit error result. The added `return PackedByteArray()` on the missing-coverage path does neither, so an incomplete `published_biome_history` or `published_vegetation_history` is reported as 'no data' with no cause logged. Ticket rule 4948331 allows showing no data, but that does not excuse dropping the logged cause required by rule 4948321. The change removes the wrong-data fallback but replaces it with a silent empty result, so a real publication gap can persist unnoticed.

findings.title: Mirror fallback survives in the inspector null-map branch
findings.description: `_season_history` in the geography cell inspector still returns the `HexCell` mirror arrays when `host._map` is null, which is the same mirror-data fallback the ticket removes from `season_history_for`. The PR leaves this sibling copy unchanged, so the front end can still read simulation mirror data in that branch.

evidence.explanation: The inspector's null-map path is a second, independent read of the mirror arrays that this PR did not update, so the ticket's 'front end reads only published data' rule is not fully enforced. The branch is likely rare in practice because the inspector normally has a map, so impact is low.
